title: A path the app hands to another program must outlive the app process
rule: When the app writes a path of its own executable or of a bundled helper into something another program keeps (a client config snippet, a login entry, a shortcut, a file association), do not derive it from current_exe() alone. On Linux inside an AppImage, current_exe() is under /tmp/.mount_*, which exists only while the app runs and is renamed at every start: use $APPIMAGE (absolute, non-empty), and when the target is a bundled helper, start the AppImage with an argument that makes the app's executable run that helper. Put the per-OS choice in fm-platform (one pure function over os, exe and env), record it in the ADR, and test it with APPIMAGE set to an absolute, an empty and a relative value, plus a test that the app's binary started with the argument does the helper's work.
rationale: E27.7 (#177): the Claude Desktop snippet named shim_beside(current_exe), so on the Linux AppImage it pointed into the temporary mount and broke when the app quit or restarted.
